name: Portugal
tagline: Cheap for EU students, but the EU route is the Portuguese one
summary: Portugal has two completely separate front doors. Non-EU students use the Estatuto do Estudante Internacional, apply straight to a university, and pay somewhere between €3,500 and €16,500 a year. EU citizens — including Danes — are legally excluded from that route and must go through the Concurso Nacional de Acesso, the same national contest Portuguese school-leavers use. The payoff is the price: the capped public tuition (propina) was €697 for 2025/26. The catch is that the national contest is built around Portuguese school exams and mostly leads to Portuguese-taught degrees.
whyConsider: Public tuition is capped: €697 a year for a licenciatura in 2025/26, and EU students pay exactly that
Nova SBE charged EU students €697 while charging international-statute students €7,500 for the same degree — the EU passport is worth real money here
Living costs outside Lisbon are among the lowest in Western Europe
A small but genuine set of English-taught bachelors in business and economics at Nova SBE and Católica Lisbon
The academic year timetable is late, so you apply after you have your IB results rather than on predictions
watchOuts: As an EU citizen you cannot use the Estatuto do Estudante Internacional — it explicitly excludes EU/EEA nationals, so the easy English-language route is closed to you

The Concurso Nacional de Acesso requires an equivalence certificate for your foreign secondary education plus provas de ingresso, which you satisfy either by sitting Portuguese national exams or by substituting homologous foreign exams
The list of foreign exams recognised as homologous is republished each year by 31 May, so you cannot plan more than a year ahead with certainty
Portuguese is required for most degrees; even the University of Porto's international route demands Portuguese at independent-user level
The whole national contest runs in late July and August, which is very late if you also need housing and a fallback

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Not defined nationally. For the national contest what matters is whether your IB subject exams can be accepted as homologous substitutes for specific provas de ingresso. Individual private institutions set their own HL rules — Nova SBE asks for at least 36 IB points with Mathematics at 6 or better for Economics and Management, and 34 points for Ocean Studies.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: For the Concurso Nacional de Acesso, foreign final exam grades are converted onto the Portuguese 0–200 scale using formulas published by DGES, with separate formulas for numerical and alphabetic grading systems.
notes: You need a certificate of equivalence confirming your foreign secondary course is equivalent to Portuguese secondary education. This is requested from a Portuguese public or private secondary school, or from the Direção-Geral da Educação.
Documents must be apostilled or consularly legalised and translated into Portuguese.

The Comissão Nacional de Acesso ao Ensino Superior publishes the list of foreign exams accepted as homologous to Portuguese provas de ingresso annually, by 31 May of the application year. Exams sat from 2022 onwards remain valid for five years.
If you request substitution of provas de ingresso by foreign exams you must apply in the earlier priority window of the first phase, not the ordinary deadline.
Private institutions such as Nova SBE and Católica accept the IB directly with their own minimum scores and do not depend on this machinery.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 1st phase applications
deadlines.notes: Candidates asking to substitute provas de ingresso with foreign exams, and those in the emigrant priority quota, must apply by 29 July 2026 instead. The 2026 calendar was approved by Despacho n.º 9359-A/2026 of 23 July. The 2027 calendar will be published separately — re-check it.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 1st phase results and enrolment
deadlines.notes: Placement lists go to the institutions the day before publication.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 2nd phase
deadlines.date: Applications 24 August to 20 September 2026, results 30 September, enrolment 1–3 October 2026
deadlines.notes: Vacancies for the second phase were announced on 1 September 2026.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 3rd phase
deadlines.date: Applications 10–12 October 2026, results 18 October, enrolment 18–20 October 2026
deadlines.notes: Vacancies announced 9 October 2026. Final complaint decisions due by 16 November 2026.

deadlines.label: Nova SBE — international bachelor admission, autumn intake
deadlines.notes: This is the direct route Nova SBE runs alongside the national contest. A spring intake also exists, with applications 10 November to 4 December 2026. Confirm 2027 dates and confirm with Nova SBE whether an EU citizen may use this route rather than the national contest.

deadlines.label: University of Porto — special contest for international students (non-EU only)
deadlines.date: Phase 1: 2 January – 6 February 2026; Phase 2: 9 February – 2 April 2026; Phase 3: 2 June – 22 July 2026
deadlines.notes: Listed for completeness. A Danish citizen is NOT eligible for this route. U.Porto offered 712 places across this contest for 2026/27.

steps: Confirm early that you are treated as an EU candidate, not an international student — Decreto-Lei n.º 36/2014 excludes EU/EEA nationals from the international-student statute.
Apply to a Portuguese secondary school or the Direção-Geral da Educação for a certificate of equivalence for your IB Diploma, with apostilled and translated documents. Start this a year ahead.
Check which provas de ingresso your target degree requires, and whether the CNAES list published by 31 May recognises an IB exam as homologous. If not, you must sit the Portuguese national exams.
Register with DGES and submit the national contest application in the first phase, using the earlier priority deadline if you are substituting foreign exams.
Rank your choices — the national contest lets you list several degree-and-institution pairs in order of preference.
Wait for the placement list, then enrol within the short window that follows (typically three or four days).
If you miss out, use the second or third phase, or apply directly to a private institution such as Católica or Nova SBE.
application.selectionNotes: The national contest is a pure ranking exercise. Each degree has a fixed number of places and a cut-off (nota do último colocado) driven by demand. Your rank comes from your converted secondary grade plus your provas de ingresso results on the 0–200 scale, weighted as the institution specifies. Private institutions and the international contest run their own selection instead.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Small. English-taught bachelor's degrees exist mainly in business and economics (Nova SBE, Católica Lisbon) with a scattering elsewhere. No official national count was found during research.
language.englishProof: Set by each institution. Nova SBE and Católica accept standard English evidence; the exact IB English grade accepted was not verified during research.
notes: Most public university degrees are taught in Portuguese, and the national contest is designed around Portuguese-taught programmes.
Even the University of Porto's contest for international students states that applicants need Portuguese at independent-user level.
Portuguese is not hard to start once you are there, but it is not optional if you go the public-university route.

tuitionEuEea.value: €697 a year (maximum propina for CTeSP, licenciatura and integrated master's), payable in at least seven monthly instalments. Institutions may not exceed the previous year's cap. Small extras apply — Nova SBE adds €36.50 for administration and insurance.

tuitionNonEu.value: Set by each institution under the Estatuto do Estudante Internacional. The University of Porto publishes a range of €3,500 to €16,500 a year; Nova SBE charges €7,500 a year for its international bachelor route.

costs.applicationFee: Nova SBE charges €70 for the international bachelor application plus a €750 enrolment fee that is deducted from tuition. No application fee was found for the national contest during research.
notes: The €697 figure is the legal maximum, not an average — some institutions charge less.
For master's and doctoral programmes institutions set their own fees; the cap only covers the first cycle.
Nationals of Portuguese-speaking (CPLP) countries can get reductions of up to 45% on international-statute fees — not relevant to a Danish student, but it explains fee tables you will see.
Living costs were not verified against an official source during this research and are deliberately left blank.

funding: Danish SU may be taken abroad for a full degree if the programme is approved — check su.dk first.

Portuguese state need-based grants (bolsas de ação social) administered by DGES and the institutions' social services; EU students are generally eligible, though the residence conditions were not verified during research.
Nova SBE and Católica run their own merit and need-based scholarships for bachelor students.
Erasmus+ for an exchange period inside the degree.
workRights: EU/EEA citizens have full labour-market access in Portugal with no permit. Non-EU students on a study residence permit may work part-time, but the exact hour limit was not verified on an official page during research.
residency: Travel on your Danish passport or ID card. For stays over three months, EU citizens register at the local câmara municipal and receive a Certificado de Registo de Cidadão da União Europeia. You will also need a NIF (tax number) from the Finanças office almost immediately — rental contracts, bank accounts and phone contracts all require it.
housing: Public universities have limited residências with means-tested places; most students rent rooms in shared flats. Lisbon rents have risen sharply and are the main practical obstacle to studying there. Porto is cheaper, and Braga, Coimbra, Aveiro and Faro are cheaper again. Because the national contest only places you in late August, look for housing before you know your result, and be ready to move quickly.
healthcare: Bring a European Health Insurance Card for short stays. Once you register as a resident and have a NIF you can register with a local health centre (centro de saúde) under the Serviço Nacional de Saúde and be assigned a family doctor.

institutions.name: Nova School of Business and Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelors in Economics, Management and Ocean Studies, taught in English
institutions.note: A beachfront campus twenty minutes from Lisbon, English-taught, and the clearest case where an EU passport changes the price from €7,500 to €697.

institutions.name: Católica Lisbon School of Business & Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught undergraduate programmes in business and economics
institutions.note: Private, internationally accredited, and the main alternative to Nova SBE for an English-taught business degree in Lisbon; fees were not verifiable during research.

institutions.name: Universidade de Lisboa
institutions.englishBachelors: Very limited at bachelor level; most first-cycle teaching is in Portuguese
institutions.note: Portugal's largest university, formed by merging the classical and technical universities of Lisbon, and home to Instituto Superior Técnico.

institutions.name: Instituto Superior Técnico
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor teaching is largely in Portuguese; English appears mainly at master's level
institutions.note: Portugal's flagship engineering school, part of ULisboa, with very high national contest cut-offs.

institutions.name: Universidade NOVA de Lisboa
institutions.englishBachelors: Concentrated in Nova SBE; limited elsewhere at bachelor level
institutions.note: A modern, decentralised university whose business school is its best-known international face.

institutions.name: ISCTE — Instituto Universitário de Lisboa
institutions.englishBachelors: Some English-taught undergraduate offer in management and international studies
institutions.note: A public university in central Lisbon with a strong social-science and business focus and a practical, employment-oriented reputation.

institutions.name: Universidade do Porto
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited at bachelor level; most first-cycle programmes are in Portuguese
institutions.note: Portugal's most complete university, with 15 faculties and around 54,000 students, in a city that is much cheaper than Lisbon.

institutions.name: Universidade do Minho
institutions.note: A research-strong university in the north with notably low living costs and a large student population relative to the city.

institutions.name: Universidade de Coimbra
institutions.note: One of Europe's oldest universities and a UNESCO World Heritage site, with the most traditional student culture in Portugal.

institutions.name: Universidade de Aveiro
institutions.note: A modern campus university with a strong engineering and materials reputation, in a small coastal city.

institutions.name: Universidade do Algarve
institutions.englishBachelors: A small English-taught offer, mainly in marine and tourism-related fields
institutions.note: The southern coastal option, cheap to live in, with genuine strength in marine science.

institutions.name: Universidade Católica Portuguesa
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught undergraduate programmes mainly through Católica Lisbon and its Porto business school
institutions.note: Portugal's main private university, which runs its own admissions and is not bound by the national contest.
